title: Study skills
summary: Evidence-based ways to learn more in less time: planning, active recall, spaced repetition and better notes.
description: Most students were never taught how to study, so they reread notes and highlight textbooks, which feel productive but don't stick. This roadmap walks through the techniques with the strongest research behind them, in the order that makes them easiest to adopt.

stages.title: Get organised
stages.summary: Know what you need to learn and when you'll learn it.

stages.title: Learn actively
stages.summary: Swap passive rereading for techniques that build lasting memory.

stages.title: Make it sustainable
stages.summary: Protect your focus and your health so you can keep going all semester.

nodes.title: How learning works
nodes.description: A short tour of how memory forms: why focused and diffuse thinking both matter, why cramming fades fast, and why struggling a little while studying is a good sign.

resources.title: Learning How to Learn (Coursera, free to audit)

nodes.title: Semester planning and time management
nodes.description: Map every deadline and exam for the semester, then plan each week backwards from them so nothing arrives as a surprise.

nodes.title: Taking useful notes
nodes.description: Take notes you can actually study from: capture the structure of a lecture, leave room for questions, and summarise each page in your own words.

nodes.title: Active recall
nodes.description: Test yourself instead of rereading. Pulling information out of memory is what strengthens it, and it shows you exactly what you don't know yet.

nodes.title: Spaced repetition
nodes.description: Review material at growing intervals (a day, a few days, a week) instead of all at once. Flashcard apps can schedule the intervals for you.

nodes.title: Reading textbooks and papers efficiently
nodes.description: Preview before you read, read with a question in mind, and stop to recall after each section, so a chapter takes one careful pass instead of three passive ones.

nodes.title: Focus and avoiding procrastination
nodes.description: Make starting easy: short timed work sessions, phone out of reach, and a clear first step. Procrastination is usually about the task feeling vague, not about laziness.

resources.title: How to tame procrastination (UNC Learning Center)

nodes.title: Sleep, exercise and stress
nodes.description: Sleep is when memories consolidate, so all-nighters undo your studying. Regular sleep, movement and breaks are part of an effective study plan.
